farm.name: IMAS Scientific Research Permit site, Tower Bay, D'Entrecasteaux Channel, Tasmania

biomass.method: grow-line length (N-22, assumed) x yield per metre (N-15)
biomass.notes: Tinderbox grew ~3.6 t on 360 m of line in ~6 months (Blue Economy CRC, Nov 2024). Tower Bay is assumed to have the same layout. Low end uses 1.2 kg/m from Biancacci et al. (2022). Ask IMAS for the Tower Bay line length and harvest weight.

scenarios.name: Central
scenarios.why: Tinderbox-sized trial (360 m of line, 10 kg/m), farm loss rates from Norwegian kelp farms.

scenarios.name: Late harvest
scenarios.why: Harvest delayed into warming water: 49% lost as pieces, as measured when a Norwegian farm harvested in August.

scenarios.name: Low growth
scenarios.why: Yield of 1.2 kg/m, the mean for farmed giant kelp at two Tasmanian sites in 2020 (Biancacci et al. 2022).

scenarios.name: Dissolved carbon upper case
scenarios.why: 33% of dissolved carbon reaches deep water, the upper boundary in Krause-Jensen & Duarte (2016).

scenarios.name: Sheltered channel
scenarios.why: Tower Bay sits in a sheltered ~15 m channel: deep export at the low end for both pieces and dissolved carbon.

scenarios.name: Full-scale farm
scenarios.why: If the whole 7.9 ha permit area held kelp at wild Tasmanian forest density (12 t/ha). Not what the trial did; shows the scale-up.

rows.label: Kelp lost as pieces before harvest (N-23)
Kelp grown per metre of line (N-15)

validation.check: Fate tree reproduces the published global budget
validation.source: Krause-Jensen & Duarte (2016), Nature Geoscience: 173 of 1,521 TgC/yr of macroalgal NPP sequestered
validation.explanation: Run with the paper's own inputs, our fate code gives 10.9% against the paper's 11.4%. The half-point gap comes from the paper rounding and listing 30% and 33% for the same DOC step, so the structure is coded correctly.

validation.check: Share of fixed carbon stored, farm vs wild forest
validation.source: Krause-Jensen & Duarte (2016) for wild forests; Duarte et al. (2017) note the share is likely smaller for farms because the crop is harvested
validation.explanation: We store about 7.5% of the carbon the kelp fixes, versus about 11% in wild forests. The difference is the harvest: about 64% of fixed carbon is taken away and sold.

validation.check: Kelp grown, compared with the sister site
validation.source: Blue Economy CRC (Nov 2024): ~3.6 t grown at Tinderbox on 360 m of line; Biancacci et al. (2022): 1.2 kg/m at other Tasmanian farms
validation.explanation: Tower Bay is assumed to match Tinderbox. Nothing public gives the Tower Bay line length or harvest weight, so this check is circular until IMAS supplies them.

validation.source: Fieler et al. (2021), farmed Saccharina in Norway: 8-13% lost by a normal harvest, 49% when delayed
validation.explanation: Central value is taken from this study, so it matches by construction. The check is that it is a farm measurement, unlike the 71% wild-forest figure used before.

validation.check: Full-scale farm: CO2 stored per hectare
validation.source: Duarte et al. (2025), Nature Climate Change: sediment burial attributable to 20 seaweed farms averaged 1.06 t CO2e/ha/yr; Bayley et al. (2017): wild Falklands giant kelp ~3.6 t CO2/ha/yr
validation.explanation: Even if the whole site were farmed, we estimate well under the 20-farm average. Wild-forest density (12 t/ha) is low for a farm, and our share buried on a sandy channel floor is small.

validation.check: Share of lost carbon released again
validation.source: N-06 cross-check: deep-ocean monitoring and lab studies report more than 90% remineralisation
validation.explanation: About 79% of the carbon lost before harvest is released again, against more than 90% from monitoring. If monitoring is right, stored carbon is roughly half our central value.

dispersion.seabed: Lines ~5 or 10 m below surface; ~15 m water over sand
dispersion.notes: Detritus that rots inside the channel releases its carbon locally; a small share of the particles settles on the sandy seabed (~15 m) and may be buried (N-05). Pieces flushed out reach Storm Bay or the southern entrance, not yet the deep ocean.

N-01.plain_english: If you dry the kelp, what fraction of what's left is carbon.
N-01.source: Reed & Brzezinski (2009): ~30% of Macrocystis dry weight is carbon (as used by Bayley et al. 2017, Falklands). SBC LTER data imply ~28% and note 20-40% variation (Rassweiler et al. 2008). 0.3217 (Reed & Miller 2021, via Gould et al. 2025) kept as the upper end; not independently re-checked 13 Oct 2026.
N-01.how_solid: GOOD species match, several consistent sources (0.28-0.32). Not measured on Tasmanian farmed kelp.
N-01.verified: 13 Oct 2026: 30% (Reed & Brzezinski 2009) confirmed via Bayley et al. 2017; ~28% from SBC LTER dataset. Changed central from 0.3217 to 0.30.

N-02.plain_english: Once a piece of kelp breaks off, how fast it rots away.
N-02.source: 0.075/day: Ecklonia radiata detritus, WA shelf (Filbee-Dexter / van der Mheen work, primary paper to verify). Lower bound: Filbee-Dexter et al. (2020), ~0.74%/day mean across 35 sites.
N-02.how_solid: WEAK - transferred across species (Ecklonia -> Macrocystis) and region (WA -> Tasmania). Published rates disagree ~10x, so sampled log-uniformly. Used only for the dispersion footprint.
N-02.verified: 13 Oct 2026: primary source for 0.075/day not found. Filbee-Dexter et al. 2024 did not use per-day rates; Smale et al. 2022 found Laminaria detritus can take >4 months to decompose (slower). Display only.

N-03.plain_english: In a wild kelp forest, how much of everything it grows breaks off as detritus. Not used for the farm, where most kelp is harvested.
N-03.source: Filbee-Dexter et al. (2024), Carbon export from seaweed forests to deep ocean sinks, Nature Geoscience: 'the fraction of the production that is exported as detritus (71% +/- 6 SE)'.
N-03.original_region: Global synthesis of wild seaweed forests
N-03.how_solid: VERIFIED value, but it applies to wild forests, not farms. Replaced in the farm model by N-23 and N-24 (13 Oct 2026). Used only in the wild-forest comparison.
N-03.verified: 13 Oct 2026: value confirmed in the paper. Misapplied to a farm before; now comparison only.

N-04.plain_english: Of the kelp pieces that drift away, how much sinks to deep water where the carbon stays locked up.
N-04.source: Krause-Jensen & Duarte (2016), Nature Geoscience 9, 737-742: about 11% of POC export (35 TgC/yr) reaches the deep sea.
N-04.how_solid: VERIFIED value and basis (fraction of POC export). Global; a sheltered 15 m channel probably exports less, hence the low end.
N-04.verified: 13 Oct 2026: 11% of POC export confirmed in the paper.

N-05.plain_english: Of the kelp pieces that stay on the shelf, how much settles into the seabed and stays there.
N-05.unit: fraction of POC retained on the shelf
N-05.source: Krause-Jensen & Duarte (2016): of the 89% of POC export retained on the shelf, 'an estimated 4.6% (14 TgC/yr) is buried in shelf sediments'.
N-05.how_solid: VERIFIED value and basis. Khushi's 0.046 was right; the old Notion row (0.04 of exported POC) had the wrong basis.
N-05.verified: 13 Oct 2026: 4.6% of shelf-retained POC confirmed in the paper.

N-06.plain_english: Everything else: eaten or rotted, so the carbon goes back to the water and air. No climate benefit.
N-06.source: Residual of the fate tree. Cross-check: deep ocean monitoring reports >90% remineralisation.
N-06.how_solid: UNCERTAIN. Our tree implies ~80%; lab studies suggest >90%. That gap is reported as uncertainty, not resolved away.
N-06.verified: 13 Oct 2026: residual, no source needed. Monitoring >90% cross-check not re-checked.

N-07.plain_english: How much detritus gets past the continental shelf edge after rotting on the way.
N-07.source: van der Mheen et al. (2024), Scientific Reports 14: 51%/yr passes the shelf edge, 17-29% after decomposition.
N-07.how_solid: WEAK - open WA shelf vs sheltered D'Entrecasteaux Channel. Used in the 'sheltered channel' sensitivity scenario.
N-07.verified: 13 Oct 2026: 51%/yr past the shelf edge, 17-29% with decomposition, confirmed (van der Mheen et al. 2024 abstract).

N-08.plain_english: When the kelp was in the water growing at Tower Bay.
N-08.source: Blue Economy CRC harvest note (22 Nov 2024): Tinderbox harvested ~6 months after outplanting; Tower Bay due for harvest the following week. Matches N-12 (14 clear scenes May-Nov 2024). Biancacci et al. (2022): April deployment, harvest window July-August in other Tasmanian sites.
N-08.how_solid: GOOD for the 2024 trial. The 2023-24 trial was killed by the summer heatwave; the 2025-26 trial ran Jun-Feb. Was 'April - August' before 13 Oct 2026, which did not match Tower Bay.
N-08.verified: 13 Oct 2026: changed from April-August to the 2024 trial window.

N-09.source: MAST Notice to Mariners M276-26(T), D'Entrecasteaux Channel, Tower Bay - Mooring Works, 4 Aug 2026.
N-09.how_solid: GOOD - authoritative government source. IMAS Scientific Research Permit site, active to 30 July 2027.
N-09.verified: 13 Oct 2026: all four corners confirmed against MAST M276-26(T) and M178-21(T). Notice describes the permit area only, not the kelp infrastructure.

N-10.source: Shoelace formula on the N-09 corners (~436 x 184 m).
N-10.how_solid: GOOD - derived from an authoritative coordinate source. ~787 Sentinel-2 pixels.
N-10.verified: 13 Oct 2026: geodesic area of N-09 = 7.873 ha (pyproj, WGS84). This is the permit area, not the area under kelp.

N-11.source: Confirmed by Jeffrey Wright (IMAS) by email: three successful Macrocystis trials at Tower Bay, last ended Feb 2026.
N-11.verified: 13 Oct 2026: IMAS email not re-checkable by Claude; CRC pages confirm Macrocystis trials at Tower Bay.

N-12.plain_english: How many clear satellite images cover the farm during a trial.
N-12.source: Copernicus Browser statistical time series, Sentinel-2 L2A over the N-09 polygon, 161 acquisitions (redone 2 Oct 2026).
N-12.how_solid: GOOD for counts. Kelp signal in NDVI is faint: satellite gives timing, not tonnes (Changes Log C-005).
N-12.verified: 13 Oct 2026: not re-checked (Copernicus counts from 2 Oct). Windows agree with the CRC harvest note.

N-13.plain_english: How much of the wet kelp is solid matter rather than water.
N-13.source: Reed & Brzezinski (2009): dry weight is 10% of wet (as used by Bayley et al. 2017); Duarte et al. (2017) use 0.1; SBC LTER data imply ~0.09; FAO (North America) 88.2% water = 0.118. Low end 0.055: Forbes et al. (2025) Tasmanian harvest records (not re-checked; may describe processed kelp).
N-13.original_region: California / North America; Tasmania for the low end
N-13.how_solid: GOOD central (four sources at 0.09-0.12). The Tasmanian 0.055 is an outlier until its method is checked. Was central 0.055 before 13 Oct 2026.
N-13.verified: 13 Oct 2026: 0.10 confirmed via Bayley et al. 2017 and Duarte et al. 2017. Forbes 2025 full text could not be opened.

N-14.plain_english: How much kelp a hectare of wild Tasmanian forest holds. Used only for the full-scale farm scenario.
N-14.source: Forbes et al. (2025) J. Phycol.: historical Tasmanian surveys 10-12 t/ha; Alginates Australia records mean 12, max 20 t/ha (not re-checked 13 Oct 2026).
N-14.how_solid: Wild-forest standing crop, not a farm yield. The trial did not cover the 7.9 ha permit area, so this is no longer used for the Tower Bay estimate (13 Oct 2026); only for the 'full-scale farm' scenario.
N-14.verified: 13 Oct 2026: not re-checked (Forbes 2025 page did not open). Use changed to scenario only.

N-15.parameter: Farm yield per metre of grow-line
N-15.plain_english: Kelp grown per metre of line on the IMAS trial leases.
N-15.unit: kg wet per metre of line (~6 months)
N-15.source: Blue Economy CRC (22 Nov 2024): ~3.6 t of Macrocystis grown at Tinderbox on 360 m of grow-line in ~6 months = 10 kg/m. Low end: Biancacci et al. (2022) Front. Mar. Sci. 9:951538, mean 1.20 kg/m (max 1.5) for farmed Macrocystis at two Tasmanian sites, 2020.
N-15.original_region: Southeast Tasmania - Tinderbox lease (same IMAS project as Tower Bay)
N-15.how_solid: GOOD project and species match. CORRECTED 13 Oct 2026: was 75 kg/m, from dividing the whole-lease 3.6 t by the 48 m harvested. The CRC note says 3.6 t was grown on 360 m in total.
N-15.verified: 13 Oct 2026: CRC article re-read; Biancacci 2022 checked.

N-16.parameter: Grow-line depth and site water depth
N-16.plain_english: How deep the lines sit and how deep the water is.
N-16.value: Lines ~5 or 10 m below surface; ~15 m water over sand
N-16.source: Blue Economy CRC, Developing Production Systems for Offshore Kelp Mariculture; Biancacci et al. (2022) Front. Mar. Sci.
N-16.how_solid: ASSUMED for Tower Bay from the same IMAS project. Explains the faint satellite signal.
N-16.verified: 13 Oct 2026: confirmed on the CRC kelp mariculture page (lines ~5 or 10 m; ~15 m water over sand at Tinderbox).

N-17.plain_english: Of the carbon that leaves the farm, how much leaves dissolved in the water rather than as pieces.
N-17.source: Khushi's durable_fraction.py (8 Oct 2026), nested structure after Krause-Jensen & Duarte (2016). Registered 13 Oct 2026 (was mislabelled N-16 in the script).
N-17.how_solid: OK. Central value from the fate script; range assumed. Khushi to confirm the primary source.
N-17.verified: 13 Oct 2026: DOC = 52% of macroalgal export confirmed in Krause-Jensen & Duarte 2016. Used only in the wild-forest comparison.

N-18.plain_english: Of the dissolved carbon the kelp releases, how much reaches deep water and stays there.
N-18.source: Upper end: Krause-Jensen & Duarte (2016), 33% of DOC exported below the mixed layer, which they call an upper boundary (their Table 1 lists 30%). Central 0.24 from Khushi's durable_fraction.py; no primary source found 13 Oct 2026.
N-18.how_solid: WEAK central: unsourced. 0.33 is a published upper boundary. Refractory DOC literature ranges 5-78% (Watanabe et al. 2020; Neves et al. 2025).
N-18.verified: 13 Oct 2026: 0.33 upper boundary confirmed; 0.24 unsourced. Type changed to Assumed.

N-19.plain_english: How many days water stays in the D'Entrecasteaux Channel before flowing out.
N-19.source: CSIRO hydrodynamic model of the D'Entrecasteaux Channel (2003-06).
N-19.how_solid: GOOD - local model. Used only for the dispersion footprint.
N-19.verified: 13 Oct 2026: confirmed, CSIRO (Marine and Freshwater Research MF09134): whole-region flushing ~20-26 days.

N-20.plain_english: Of the water leaving the channel, how much goes north to Storm Bay rather than south.
N-20.source: CSIRO D'Entrecasteaux Channel model: most water leaves north into Storm Bay, a smaller share south. Exact split not published; 0.75 assumed.
N-20.how_solid: ASSUMED split; direction is from the CSIRO model. Display only, does not change the carbon estimate.
N-20.verified: 13 Oct 2026: direction confirmed (predominantly northward, small share south); CSIRO gives no percentage, so 0.75 stays assumed. CSIRO also notes the northern channel connects poorly with the rest.

N-21.plain_english: The shape of growth through the season: slow start, fast middle, levelling off.
N-21.unit: logistic rate per month (midpoint at mid-season)
N-21.source: Assumed logistic shape, scaled so end-of-season biomass equals N-10 x N-14. Satellite gives timing only (C-005).
N-21.how_solid: ASSUMED shape. Season totals don't depend on it; only the month-by-month split does.
N-21.verified: 13 Oct 2026: assumed shape, no source needed; season totals don't depend on it.

N-22.plain_english: How many metres of kelp line were in the water.
N-22.source: ASSUMED equal to Tinderbox, the sister site in the same IMAS/CRC project: 360 m of grow-line on three 18 m rings and a 60 m array (Blue Economy CRC kelp mariculture page; harvest note 22 Nov 2024).
N-22.how_solid: ASSUMED. The single biggest unknown. Ask Jeff Wright (IMAS) for the Tower Bay line length and harvest weight; both would replace this and N-15.
N-22.verified: 13 Oct 2026: new. Replaces 'whole 7.9 ha permit area is kelp'.

N-23.parameter: Kelp lost from the farm as pieces
N-23.plain_english: Share of what the farm grows that breaks off and drifts away before harvest.
N-23.source: Fieler et al. (2021) Front. Mar. Sci. 8:632725, farmed Saccharina latissima, Norway: 8-13% of produced dry weight lost by a normal harvest; 49% when harvest was delayed to August.
N-23.how_solid: OK. Measured on real kelp farms, but a different species and region. Tower Bay was harvested in November, later in the season than Biancacci et al. recommend, so losses may sit above the central value.
N-23.verified: 13 Oct 2026: new; checked in the paper.

N-24.plain_english: Share of the carbon the kelp fixes that leaks out dissolved in the water.
N-24.source: Central: Krause-Jensen & Duarte (2016), DOC export 355 of 1,521 TgC/yr NPP (23%). Range: Neves et al. (2025), farmed Saccharina latissima, DOC release 12-29% of fixed carbon (via SINTEF summary).
N-24.original_region: Global; Norway for the farm range
N-24.how_solid: OK. Consistent central and farm range, but no Macrocystis farm measurement.
N-24.verified: 13 Oct 2026: new; K-J&D figures checked in the paper, Neves et al. via SINTEF summary.
